title: Test Fixtures
concept: Test fixtures provide reusable setup and teardown for test environments
why: Many tests need the same initial state: a database connection, a temporary file, a configured object. Copy-pasting setup code into every test is brittle and verbose. Fixtures encapsulate this boilerplate so tests focus on the behavior being verified, not environmental plumbing.
theory: XIOM supports fixtures through the `@before_each` and `@after_each` attributes on functions within a test module. `@before_each` runs before every test in the module; `@after_each` runs after. Fixture data can be passed to tests via a `TestContext` struct. For shared setup across an entire module (once, not per-test), use `@before_all` and `@after_all`. Fixtures are scoped to their enclosing module.
tips: Use fixtures for expensive setup (DB connections, file handles)
Keep fixtures simple — they should prepare state, not test behavior
Fixture functions must return the type that tests expect as a parameter
common_mistakes: Sharing mutable state between tests via fixtures (tests run in parallel)
Writing fixtures that have side effects without corresponding teardown
Assuming fixtures run in a specific order
